summary: CRITICAL F6 REGRESSION FOUND. EmissionEntryForm completely crashes on render with 'ReferenceError: buildDecisionContext is not defined'. The Add Emission dialog opens but immediately throws a React Uncaught runtime error overlay, blocking ALL Step 1 controls (facility/scope/category/fuel labels missing from DOM). Form is non-functional end-to-end. Testing HALTED — cannot proceed with Save/Edit/C7/DynamicFieldRenderer/getFieldUnits/preview flows because the dialog body never renders. Pre-existing baseline (iteration_82) was clean; this is a NEW regression introduced by the F6 lift of handleSubmit into useEmissionSubmit.

ui_bugs.issue: ReferenceError: buildDecisionContext is not defined. The ctx object passed to useEmissionSubmit({...}) uses property shorthand { evaluateFormula, buildDecisionContext, buildDecisionInputs, extractInputsForCalcEngine, ... } but buildDecisionContext and extractInputsForCalcEngine are NOT defined in EmissionEntryForm scope. They are module-level exports from /app/frontend/src/modules/emissions/categories/shared/Scope1Create.js (and Scope3FlatCreate.js etc.) accessed via the categoryRegistry, never as local component helpers. JavaScript evaluates the shorthand `buildDecisionContext` at line 2496 and throws ReferenceError before the function component can return its JSX — so the dialog renders the red runtime-error overlay instead of Step 1 controls.

critical_code_review_comments: [CRITICAL — F6 regression, exact RCA] EmissionEntryForm.js:2496 passes `buildDecisionContext` and `extractInputsForCalcEngine` to useEmissionSubmit() via property shorthand. Neither identifier exists in the component scope (verified via grep — only `buildDecisionInputs` (line 1204) and `evaluateFormula` (line 1540) are defined locally). At useEmissionSubmit.js:45-46 the hook also destructures these from ctx, BUT it never uses the destructured values — every call site uses module-method access: `dispatchActiveModule.buildDecisionContext(data, baseCtx)` (line 589), `yearlyMod.buildDecisionContext(...)` (line 340), `dispatchActiveModule.extractInputsForCalcEngine(...)` (line 588), `yearlyMod.extractInputsForCalcEngine(...)` (line 339). FIX (1-line, byte-identical behaviour): remove `buildDecisionContext` and `extractInputsForCalcEngine` from BOTH the ctx shorthand at EmissionEntryForm.js:2496 AND the destructure at useEmissionSubmit.js:45-46. They are dead ctx params.

[POSITIVE — defensible refactor pattern otherwise] The other ~50 ctx props (state slots, setters, computed values, evaluateFormula, buildDecisionInputs, canProceedToStep, getAuthHeader, onSuccess, getActualYearForMonth, editingEmission) ARE all defined in EmissionEntryForm and correctly destructured. Only these two stray identifiers are broken.

rca_of_the_issue: ROOT CAUSE: F6 lift-and-shift refactor moved handleSubmit body into a new useEmissionSubmit hook that takes a ctx object. While building the ctx at EmissionEntryForm.js:2496 the main agent listed `buildDecisionContext` and `extractInputsForCalcEngine` as property shorthand (the same way as `evaluateFormula` and `buildDecisionInputs` which ARE local). But buildDecisionContext/extractInputsForCalcEngine are NOT local to EmissionEntryForm — they are module-level exports on the categoryRegistry modules (Scope1Create.js / Scope3FlatCreate.js / etc.) and are accessed inside the hook via `dispatchActiveModule.buildDecisionContext(...)` / `yearlyMod.extractInputsForCalcEngine(...)`. JavaScript evaluates the shorthand identifier at object-literal construction time, throws ReferenceError, React's render boundary catches it and displays the red runtime-error overlay over the entire dialog body. REPRO: login as goyalsomil@hotmail.com → /emissions → click 'Add Emission' → red overlay 'buildDecisionContext is not defined' appears immediately. MITIGATION: delete those two identifiers from BOTH the ctx shorthand (EmissionEntryForm.js:2496) AND the ctx destructure inside the hook (useEmissionSubmit.js:45-46). They are dead params — the hook accesses these functions only via the resolved module object, not via ctx. Behaviour stays byte-identical after the removal.
